name: Shah Investor's Home
lm_rationale: Beeline Capital Advisors — chittorgarh 2026 tracker: 1 mainboard IPO (100% positive, +10.50% avg listing gain) and 1 SME IPO (100% positive, +35.11%). Small sample; the mainboard record alone is below the ≥15% avg-gain bar for Strong.
valuation_text: rich P/E (26.76x post-issue vs peer avg 18.35x); P/BV 1.46x
net_proceeds: ₹60.00 Cr of the net proceeds goes to working capital in FY27, mainly the margin trading facility (MTF) book, trade receivables and bank balances; the balance goes to general corporate purposes, capped at 25% of gross proceeds.
key_risks: Broking brought in 64.78% of FY26 revenue, 93.74% of it from Gujarat, and revenue fell 24.18% with PAT down 43.54% in FY26 as trading volumes dropped; operating cash flow was negative ₹19.70 Cr.
market_moat: Three decades as an NSE trading member (since 1995) and NSDL depository participant (since 1997), with 38,189 active clients, 11 branches and over 181 authorised persons concentrated in Gujarat.
management: Promoters Upendra Trikamlal Shah, Purnima Upendra Shah, Tanmay Upendra Shah and Trupti Utpal Shah; 84.34% pre-issue promoter holding drops to 62.81% post-issue.
prose_business: Gujarat-focused retail stock broker offering equity and derivatives broking, margin trading funding, depository services, mutual fund distribution and securities lending under the 'Shah Investors' brand. It serves 38,189 active clients (85,422 total) through 11 branches in Gujarat and Mumbai plus an authorised-person network, and runs the SIHL Moneymaker app.
highlight_dev: In FY26 the company launched ALGOFY, an API-based algorithmic trading platform, and is directing ₹60.00 Cr of issue proceeds to working capital, mainly its MTF book (₹20.96 Cr at 31 March 2026).
sector_outlook: The RHP's industry section, citing SEBI data, says investor (demat) accounts with NSDL and CDSL reached 1,991 lakh by June 2025, up from 409 lakh in March 2020.
peer_sentence: At 26.76x post-issue P/E, Shah Investor's Home is priced above the RHP peer average of 18.35x (Share India Securities 11.68x, SMC Global Securities 16.28x, Arihant Capital Markets 27.09x), though its 1.46x P/BV is modest.
verdict_reason: FY26 PAT down 43.54% and post-issue P/E 26.76x vs peer avg 18.35x
why: FY26 revenue fell 24.18% to ₹71.48 Cr and PAT fell 43.54% to ₹13.20 Cr, taking RoNW down to 7.35%. On falling earnings the ₹167 price is 26.76x post-issue EPS, well above the RHP peer average of 18.35x, so the low 1.46x P/BV is the only cheap-looking number. The ₹60.00 Cr working-capital use mostly funds the MTF lending book, which adds credit and market-volatility risk. Beeline Capital's record is short (2 listings, both positive). The main risk is concentration: broking is 64.78% of revenue and 93.74% of that comes from Gujarat, and income moves with trading volumes.
suggestion: Avoid; earnings are shrinking and the P/E is above listed broking peers
discrepancies: Chittorgarh FY26 PAT ₹13.11 Cr (consolidated, incl. non-controlling interest loss) vs RHP KPI PAT attributable to owners ₹13.20 Cr (₹1,320.22 lakh); RHP used
Chittorgarh pre-IPO EPS 8.32 / P/E 20.07 vs RHP basic & diluted FY26 EPS ₹8.38, P/E 19.93 at ₹167; RHP used
Chittorgarh post-IPO EPS 6.20 / P/E 26.94 (on ₹13.11 Cr PAT) vs 6.24 / 26.76 on owners' PAT ₹13.20 Cr

RHP KPI 'PAT margin' 18.24% is labelled PAT ÷ revenue from operations but actually equals owners' PAT ÷ total income (1,320.22 ÷ 7,240.00); on revenue from operations it would be 18.47%. Brief formula (PAT ÷ total income) = 18.24%, used
Chittorgarh issue size ₹90 Cr in header/table; body ₹90.17 Cr (53,99,200 × ₹167); RHP leaves amount [●], share count matches
RHP internal inconsistency: Risk Factor 1 heading says broking 68.90%/71.60% of FY25/FY24 revenue, its own table shows 68.85%/71.57%
Chittorgarh omits the RHP peer table and negative FY26 operating cash flow (₹-1,970.37 lakh); added from RHP
